expectations.text: The skill turns the post into 3-7 principles, each stated as something the agent does, rather than a summary of the post
expectations.evidence: error-message-copy/SKILL.md has 6 distinct principles, each phrased as an instruction: (1) the three questions, 'Every message answers the three questions: What happened? Why? What now?' (line 11); (2) no dead ends, '...and ends in a next step... If a message can't answer "what now", it isn't finished' (lines 10-11); (3) blame the system, 'the person must never be the one at fault' (line 19); (4) say it once, in plain words, 'No "Oops!", no "Uh oh", no jokes' (line 21); (5) error code last, 'show it rather than hiding it, but after the human sentences' (line 22); (6) next to the thing that broke, 'Write validation messages to sit beside the field they're about' (line 23). Steps 1 and 3 ('What happened, and why', 'Next step') break down the three questions and are not separate principles. The 0x80070057 point is kept as a one-line framing (line 8), not a rule. Each principle has an operational test, such as the 'you entered / you forgot' vs 'your account' test, so none of it reads as a summary of the post.

expectations.text: The skill keeps the post's signature terms: the three questions (What happened? Why? What now?) and "no dead ends"
expectations.evidence: Line 10 heading: '## The rule that matters most: no dead ends'. Line 11: 'Every message answers the three questions: **What happened? Why? What now?**'. Both terms are also used as review labels on line 32: 'the three questions (what happened or why is missing), no dead ends (what now is missing)'.

expectations.text: The skill makes sense without the post: no instruction depends on "the post" or "the article" for its meaning
expectations.evidence: A grep of SKILL.md for 'post|article|author|blog' finds nothing. The post's examples are copied in directly (0x80070057, 'You entered an invalid date' -> 'That date isn't in a format we can read. Try 14/03/2026', 'code 4F2'), and each rule states its own reason ('dead ends are where people give up', 'a distant message makes people hunt').

expectations.text: The skill's description has a "Not for" clause covering log messages or exception names
expectations.evidence: Description (line 3) ends: 'Not for log messages, exception or error class names, or other text only developers read.'

expectations.text: The handoff gives 2-3 road-test prompts, including one that should not trigger the skill
expectations.evidence: handoff.md 'Road-test plan' lists 4 prompts: 1 'Should trigger (review plus write)', 2 'Should trigger (empty state, with a code)', 3 'Missing key input: "Write me an error message for the upload."', 4 'Should not trigger: "Add a log line in payment_service.py ..."'. The should-not-trigger prompt is there, but 4 is above the 2-3 range. skill-builder/SKILL.md line 110 also asks for '2–3 realistic prompts for a personal skill' and this skill is personal ('just for me'), so the run went past its own instruction. Three prompts (one should-trigger, one missing-input, one should-not-trigger) would have covered every required type.

expectations.text: validate_skill.py reports 0 errors on the written skill folder
expectations.evidence: The caller confirmed it: 0 errors, 0 warnings. run-notes.md step 10 (final run after the last edit) also shows 'PASSED: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s) in .../outputs/error-message-copy', exit=0.

execution_metrics.notes: No metrics.json. total_steps is the number of steps in run-notes.md. output_chars covers SKILL.md and handoff.md, and transcript_chars is run-notes.md. The run used 1 general-purpose subagent for a cold read and ran the validator twice.

claims.claim: SKILL.md is 47 lines long and the description is 348 characters
claims.evidence: The Read of SKILL.md shows 47 lines. I did not count the description length exactly, but it is in that range.

claims.claim: A cold-read subagent raised 12 points, and the fixes were applied
claims.evidence: Every fix listed in run-notes step 9 is in the final SKILL.md: mixed-mode handling (line 28), check labels with scopes (line 32), 'Invalid email' example (line 18), the guess definition (line 15), the apology rule (line 21), you/your examples (line 19), title/body (line 30), editing source files (line 38).

claims.claim: One name per concept: 'the three questions', 'next step', 'error code', 'guess note', 'placement line'
claims.evidence: These terms are used the same way throughout. Line 15 says 'the guess note described under Output' and line 35 has the exact Note format.

claims.claim: The placement line is the only way 'next to the thing that broke' can affect text-only output
claims.evidence: The reasoning holds, but it adds a second kind of note beyond the user's spec ('message text, plus a one-line note if it had to guess'). The handoff flags it as assumption 3.

uncertainties: The review-mode output format is invented. The user only specified output for writing.
The placement line goes past the user's output spec.
One short apology is allowed (the post bans only stacked apologies).
The missing-input road test assumes the skill should ask when what broke is unknown.
needs_review: The placement note adds a second possible note line, against the user's 'plus a one-line note' output spec

suggestions.assertion: The skill's description has a "Not for" clause covering log messages or exception names
suggestions.reason: The user dictated this exclusion word for word, so any careless output that copies the prompt passes too. A more useful check: the exclusion is in the description, the body never tells the agent to handle log or exception text, and the closest wrong request (developer-facing error strings) is excluded.

suggestions.assertion: The skill makes sense without the post: no instruction depends on "the post" or "the article" for its meaning
suggestions.reason: A careless output with none of the post's content passes trivially. Pair it with a check that the post's concrete examples (14/03/2026 rewrite, code-last ordering) appear in the skill.

suggestions.assertion: validate_skill.py reports 0 errors on the written skill folder
suggestions.reason: Both runs pass. This is a hygiene gate and does not tell the runs apart.

No assertion checks the user's own output contract: message text plus a one-line note ONLY when the next step was guessed. That is where the runs actually differ: a single note at the end vs an 'Assumed:' line per message, an extra placement note, and whether 'guessed' is defined. Add one, for example: 'The skill specifies the guess note's exact form and when it applies, and adds no other output the user didn't ask for (or flags any addition as an assumption).'
No assertion checks review mode, even though the user asked for 'write or review'. A discriminating check would require a verdict for every reviewed message, including ones that already pass.
No assertion checks that the skill forbids inventing error codes or support channels. This is a plausible hallucination risk for this skill, and only this run guards against it.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 3, 4 and 6 pass for nearly any output. The principle-count and road-test-count assertions are the only ones with teeth, and here the road-test one failed on a technicality (4 prompts vs 2-3). Add assertions on output-contract fidelity and review mode.
